title: New chart panel: Relative Strength Index (RSI)
description: Surface RSI (backend-indicator-rsi) as a new oscillator panel or an additional line on the existing OscillatorChart, alongside Stochastic. Explain, not just plot, the comparison Elder himself draws: RSI is closing-price-only and tends to give earlier/cleaner signals than Stochastic on the same data -- worth stating in the help content so a user understands why both exist rather than treating it as redundant. Per the project's established explanatory pattern (common/InfoBalloon, common/MetricHelp, metricHelpContent.ts, signalExplanation.ts, docs/tasks/frontend-stock-detail-metric-help.json), every new visual element this task adds must be explainable, not just displayed: a help affordance (reuse MetricHelp where it fits) that states what the metric/signal is, how it relates to Dr. Elder's methodology, and, where meaningful, an explanation of the CURRENT value shown -- not a static definition alone. Add an entry to metricHelpContent.ts's registry rather than inventing a parallel explanation mechanism.

checklist.step: Decide whether RSI becomes a new OscillatorChart variant or an additional series on the existing Stochastic panel; record.
Implement, following existing chart component conventions.
MetricHelp content explaining RSI, its formula in plain terms, and the RSI-vs-Stochastic comparison from the book.
Tests + Storybook story; confirm 90% coverage gate holds.

decisions.decision: RSI is plotted as a second `LineSeries` sharing Stochastic %K's existing pane 0/y-axis on `OscillatorChart.tsx` (dashed, `theme.palette.secondary.main`), not a fourth separate Lightweight Charts pane, and not a new stat card on `IndicatorsPanel.tsx`.
decisions.rationale: The whole point of this task, per its own description, is exposing Elder's side-by-side RSI-vs-Stochastic comparison (closing-price-only, 'less noisy', earlier signals) -- both are already bounded 0-100 oscillators computed over near-identical windows, so sharing one axis lets a user actually compare the two lines directly on the same chart, which is exactly what the book's own comparison shows. A fourth pane would force the user to mentally overlay two separate charts to see the same relationship, defeating the point. A new IndicatorsPanel StatCard was rejected as out of this task's explicit scope ('surface RSI ... as a new oscillator panel or an additional line on the existing OscillatorChart') and as a redundant second surface for a value already covered by the chart's own MetricHelp legend row -- see the next decision.

decisions.decision: RSI reuses Stochastic's existing 30/70 dashed reference lines on the shared pane rather than adding a second, RSI-specific pair of price lines at the same 30/70 levels.
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md itself documents 30/70 as the shared overbought/oversold reference line for both Stochastic and RSI (used identically by the divergence detector's `beyond_reference_line` check for both indicators) -- drawing a second, visually-identical pair of dashed lines at the exact same y-values would only add clutter with no new information, and Lightweight Charts' price lines are shared visual elements on a pane's y-axis anyway (there's no way to visually distinguish 'this 30-line is for RSI' vs 'this 30-line is for Stochastic' even if drawn twice). Rejected a second RSI-only pair of reference lines as redundant, and rejected omitting reference lines entirely as inconsistent with how Stochastic's own lines already work on this pane.

decisions.decision: RSI's line color is `theme.palette.secondary.main` (purple), dashed (`LineStyle.Dashed`), distinct from Stochastic's solid `theme.palette.primary.main` (blue) -- not colored by sign/zone the way Force Index/MACD Histogram bars are.
decisions.rationale: RSI and Stochastic %K are both single continuous lines on a shared axis, so the priority is visual distinguishability between the two lines themselves (solid-vs-dashed plus a clearly different hue), not per-point coloring -- unlike Force Index/MACD Histogram, which are histograms colored by sign because each bar's sign is itself the signal being read. `theme.palette.secondary.main` was already defined in the theme (not a new color needing its own decision/approval) and is visually distinct from every other color already used on this pane (primary blue for Stochastic, signal buy/sell green/red for the histograms' zero-baseline reference lines).

decisions.decision: No new `components/common/` component was introduced (RSI reuses the existing `common/MetricHelp` as-is), so no new Storybook story was added -- `OscillatorChart.tsx` itself is a `features/stocks/components/` component and has never had a Storybook story (per Frontend.md §4, only `components/common/` needs one).
decisions.rationale: The add-frontend-feature skill's Storybook requirement (step 5) is scoped to `components/common/` components specifically -- OscillatorChart is, and remains, a feature-specific chart component wired to a live TanStack Query hook, the same category PriceChart/StockCharts/IndicatorsPanel already fall into without their own stories. Adding a story for a feature component here would be inconsistent with every other chart component in this codebase and isn't what the skill actually requires.

decisions.decision: `rsiHelp.interpretValue`'s RSI-vs-Stochastic agreement threshold is set at a 10-point gap (values within 10 points of each other read as 'broadly agreeing'; further apart reads as 'diverging', naming the closing-price-only reason).
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md doesn't specify a numeric agreement/divergence threshold between the two oscillators -- this is a presentation-layer judgment call for the help text's current-value interpretation, not a methodology rule. 10 points (out of the shared 0-100 scale) was picked as a reasonable 'same reading, different precision' band, wide enough to not flag routine noise as a meaningful divergence but narrow enough that a real divergence (e.g. one oscillator oversold while the other is still neutral) gets called out, which is exactly the situation Elder's own 'RSI signals earlier' comparison describes. This only affects explanatory text, not any chart rendering or signal logic, so a different threshold would be a low-risk follow-up if review disagrees.
